parent.title: Epic: Agent-facing scene inspection and precise selection
parent.description: Extend the procedural editor command surface for reliable inspect, pick, select, capture and verify loops. Shared selection state; typed stable IDs; exact scene/view revisions; native Windows acceptance. Operator-requested Matter Engine workload for AQ integration acceptance.

nodes.title: Define discoverable agent command and response contracts
nodes.description:
Use the existing MatterEditor app-thread CommandRegistry, FIFO transport, SelectionSet, picker and procedural authoring model. Read CLAUDE.md and docs/agent/control-surface.md plus qa-cookbook.md first. Native Windows acceptance uses tools/build-windows-from-wsl.sh and the MSVC CMake graph, not MinGW. Preserve existing FIFO verbs and machine-readable stdout. Reuse source-of-truth libraries; no copied or symlinked sibling sources. Work only in the AQ-assigned branch/workspace. Record exact checks, resulting Git head, PR, and unresolved limitations on the AQ task. This graph is a real acceptance workload for recursive feature-branch integration: no direct main push or ad hoc merge of sibling branches. If a prerequisite artifact has not reached your branch, report the exact missing revision through AQ instead of silently copying it.

Document and implement a versioned request/result envelope over the existing control surface, including a scriptable client entry point. Reconcile existing ticketed registry acknowledgements rather than inventing an unrelated command dispatcher.
acceptance: Expose command discovery/help/schema with arguments and availability; unknown or unsupported commands fail explicitly.
Correlate request IDs, command tickets and one terminal result; keep logs separate from parseable JSON output and preserve legacy text/FIFO commands.
Define typed object identity {kind,id} using lossless string IDs, scene/session generation, scene revision, selection revision and frame/view identity.
Bound request parsing, output size and wait time; distinguish invalid input, not-ready, not-found, stale revision, timeout and execution failure.
Test partial/malformed input, escaping, duplicate request IDs, mixed logs, delayed completion, disconnect/reconnect and native Windows file polling.

Provide bounded scene enumeration and exact object inspection that joins authored entities and baked roots while preserving their distinct identity namespaces.
acceptance: List objects with pagination/filtering and deterministic ordering; return scene revision and lossless typed IDs.
Inspect kind, authored name/path where available, world bounds/transform, visibility, selected/primary state, and supported operations.
Expose explicit provenance availability rather than fabricate source paths; do not expose Flecs handles as stable authored IDs.
Test overlapping numeric IDs across kinds, deleted objects, unloaded roots, rebakes and world switching.

Extend the single viewer::SelectionSet through typed app-thread commands. Selection is editor state; selection commands do not modify procedural source or object geometry.
acceptance: Implement replace, add, remove, toggle and clear with a deterministic primary-selection policy; support mixed entities and baked roots.
List selected objects and primary with typed IDs and revisions; repeated add/remove/clear have explicit idempotent results.
Validate the whole request before mutation; stale generation or invalid IDs do not silently retarget reused IDs.
GUI selection and command selection share exactly one SelectionSet and update existing outlines/gizmo state.
Cover rebake pruning, world switch, missing IDs, duplicate IDs and primary removal in focused tests.

Accept viewport coordinates as a command and use the same camera/picking semantics as interactive selection. No OS mouse injection or second competing ray-caster.
acceptance: Define viewport-local logical pixels versus framebuffer pixels explicitly; report viewport rectangle, scale, camera and frame identity.
Support a read-only pick and pick-and-select with replace/add/toggle modes; return hit/miss, typed ID, world hit position and available geometric detail.
Allow an expected screenshot/frame/view revision and reject stale coordinates when the view changed; document any supported current-frame mode.
Test perspective/orthographic if supported, resize/DPI, viewport offsets, occlusion, out-of-bounds coordinates and unavailable/unloaded geometry.
Ensure command and actual GUI picking resolve the same objects in a deterministic fixture scene.

Connect existing screenshot and camera commands to structured scene/view metadata so an agent can close the visual feedback loop.
acceptance: Return screenshot path, dimensions, viewport bounds, frame/camera/scene/selection revisions and completion only after a successful presented-frame capture.
Provide focus/frame selected or exact object ID using existing camera/bounds behavior; return not-found/not-ready explicitly.
Provide optional selected-object overlay/ID annotations without changing authored content; preserve existing screenshot commands.
Test capture timeout, failed presentation, resize and pick-from-capture coherence.
